comparisons.peer_topic: Client segment AI adoption and historical performance risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Client segment revenue depends on AI PC adoption; while AMD is building AI capabilities like Ryzen AI into Client products, adoption pace is uncertain; past revenue declines in Client and Gaming segments have been driven by form factor changes, competition, and replacement cycle changes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose risks and strategies specifically tied to the adoption of AI-capable processors in the Client (PC) segment. Intel highlights the introduction of 'Intel Core Ultra processors, powering the latest AI PCs' and 'Intel Xeon 6 processors' as part of its brand portfolio strategy to drive preference and aid consumer choices. Similarly, AMD explicitly states that its Client segment revenue 'will depend in part on the market's adoption of AI PCs' and notes the active building of AI capabilities like 'Ryzen AI PC processors,' while warning that there is 'no assurance about the rate and pace of adoption.' While Intel frames this as a positive brand differentiation and product launch, AMD frames it as a demand-side risk and uncertainty regarding market acceptance.

sentences.text: Our global marketing objectives are to build a strong, well-known, differentiated, and meaningful Intel corporate brand that drives preference with businesses and consumers, and to offer a limited number of meaningful and valuable brands in our portfolio to aid businesses and consumers in making informed choices about technology purchases.
This year we introduced our new Intel Core Ultra processors, powering the latest AI PCs, and our Intel Xeon 6 processors, built with AI acceleration in every core.
Also, our Client segment revenue is focused on the consumer desktop and notebook PC segments and will depend in part on the market's adoption of AI PCs.
We are actively building AI capabilities into all our Client products, such as Ryzen AI PC processors, but there can be no assurance about the rate and pace of adoption of such product offerings.
